description: Floating-point division followed by ceiling can push a limiting dimension above its maximum, and patch alignment amplifies the overshoot.
trigger: Call the new helper with input_size=(230,1), max_size=(224,192), patch_size=(16,32).
expected_behavior: Return patch-aligned dimensions no larger than (224,192), as promised by the bounding-box contract.
actual_behavior: The scalar transcription produces (240,32): the computed limiting dimension rounds up to 225 before alignment. The source has no final clamp. No repository callers were found in the parent, and the diff introduces none, so reach is limited to direct prospective or external use. At 234 the first integrated caller is Mistral3 preprocessing, reached by get_image_embeddings; scalar transcription gives 1568x1008 for 1541x1000 at longest edge 1540 and alignment 28. Replacement 234/002 follows the same overflow into the precomputed vision RoPE table: 28x1541 becomes 28x1568, a (112,2) feature grid reaches position 12211 against 12100 rows. Source and scalar evidence only; no GPU fault observed.

finding.description: The new image pipeline inherits an unclamped floating-point resize overflow, allowing feature positions outside its precomputed RoPE table.
finding.trigger: Use an otherwise valid processor configuration with longest_edge=1540, patch_size=14 and spatial_merge_size=2, then call Mistral3VisionModel.get_image_embeddings with a 28×1541 image.
finding.expected_behavior: Resize to merge-aligned dimensions within the configured maximum, keeping every generated position ID inside the angle table.
finding.actual_behavior: The scalar transcription rounds the limiting height to 1541 before alignment and returns 28×1568. The new caller therefore builds features_size=(112,2), with position IDs reaching 12211 despite only 12100 table rows. Neither the image caller nor the inspected CUDA wrapper validates row bounds. Source reach is the new get_image_embeddings → preprocess → helper → vision attention path; the parent had no caller of the sizing helper. No resulting image-library behavior or GPU fault was observed.
